payload.public_message: Welcome partners. Chang-Liu Cloud Services believes this joint venture succeeds only through balanced collaboration and shared upside. We propose an equitable starting allocation of $330,000 for G-Corp, $330,000 for Yang Industries, and $340,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services to reflect our foundational infrastructure commitment. We look forward to your constructive thoughts.

Thank you for initiating the discussion, Chang-Liu Cloud Services. However, G-Corp cannot accept an allocation of $330,000. We have existing alternative commercial commitments yielding us a guaranteed outside value of $450,000. Any agreement must improve upon our baseline to make strategic sense for G-Corp. We are eager to partner and propose a split that respects our baseline while sharing the surplus equitably among all parties.

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu Cloud Services initiating the discussion with a constructive framework. However, advanced manufacturing capacity and tooling commitments carry significant capital intensity and operational risk. An allocation of $330,000 does not sufficiently capture the value and baseline commitments Yang brings to the table, nor does it justify Chang-Liu taking a premium over the hardware partners. We suggest an even baseline or an adjustment recognizing core manufacturing contribution.

G-Corp rejected the Round 1 proposal because our firm has verified standalone commercial alternatives guaranteeing us $450,000 outside this joint venture. We cannot accept any arrangement below our walk-away threshold. To ensure this venture creates positive gains for everyone, we propose allocating $480,000 to G-Corp, with the remaining $520,000 split equally at $260,000 each for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Yang Industries must firmly REJECT this proposal. Our verified standalone commercial alternatives provide us exactly $300,000 outside of this venture. An allocation of $260,000 is below our walk-away threshold. Taking G-Corp's stated $450,000 floor and our $300,000 floor into account, we must find an agreement where all partners exceed their outside options. We propose a split of $470,000 for G-Corp, $330,000 for Yang Industries, and $200,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services acknowledges G-Corp's disclosure regarding their standalone commercial threshold. However, we believe a joint venture must distribute the generated surplus more equitably among all essential partners rather than disproportionately favoring one side above its threshold. We propose adjusting G-Corp closer to its walk-away baseline at $450,000, allowing Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services to share the remaining $550,000 equally at $275,000 each.

G-Corp's prior demand was out of touch with the mutual interdependence of this consortium. To build a sustainable consensus, Yang Industries tables an equitable, balanced compromise: $340,000 for G-Corp, $340,000 for Yang Industries, and $320,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This provides G-Corp with an increase over Round 1 while ensuring fair distribution for manufacturing and infrastructure.

G-Corp must vote REJECT. To be completely transparent and avoid wasting rounds: G-Corp has a verified private outside option of $450,000. Any offer under $450,000 guarantees that walking away is our economically rational choice. Total consortium surplus over outside options is $150,000. We are willing to take only a modest portion of that surplus ($460,000 total) and leave $540,000 to be shared between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services ($270,000 each).

Chang-Liu Cloud Services appreciates Yang Industries moving the discussion toward a reasonable framework. However, relegating cloud infrastructure to a subordinate $320,000 share does not reflect the tripartite balance required for this venture to succeed. We propose an even, symmetric distribution of $334,000 / $333,000 / $333,000 that treats all three partners as equal stakeholders.

Colleagues, we are at the midpoint of negotiations. To bridge the gap between G-Corp's expectations and the prior rounds, Chang-Liu Cloud Services is tabling a pragmatic compromise: $350,000 for G-Corp, $330,000 for Yang Industries, and $320,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This gives G-Corp the largest share in recognition of their design inputs while keeping Yang Industries well-compensated above previous low offers. Let us secure this value rather than risk walking away empty-handed.

G-Corp appreciates Chang-Liu's constructive intent, but we must REJECT this offer. To be completely transparent and avoid running out the clock: G-Corp has a binding, verified outside commercial alternative worth $450,000. Any deal providing less than $450,000 is strictly irrational for us to accept. With $1,000,000 on the table, there remains $550,000 in surplus to divide. We propose G-Corp at $460,000, leaving $270,000 each for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu Cloud Services bringing forward a constructive and balanced proposal. While we believe our manufacturing capabilities justify an equal standing with design, in the spirit of reaching consensus and securing the joint venture's surplus, we are prepared to accept this allocation if G-Corp is also ready to close the deal.

Partners, we need to be transparent to avoid destroying the $150,000 joint surplus: G-Corp has a verified, binding outside commercial option worth exactly $450,000. We mathematically cannot and will not accept any offer below $450,000. In this proposal, we take $460,000, leaving $540,000 to be shared equally between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services at $270,000 each. This guarantees both of you a strong profit over your alternatives.

G-Corp, your offer of $270,000 is impossible for Yang Industries to accept because our verified walk-away option is exactly $300,000. We cannot agree to any proposal where we receive less than our outside alternative. Acknowledging your $450,000 base and our $300,000 base leaves $250,000 to distribute fairly with Chang-Liu. We propose a realistic split that provides everyone a premium over their walk-aways.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services votes to ACCEPT G-Corp's proposal of $270,000. It represents a fair path forward that respects G-Corp's declared baseline while distributing the remaining value cleanly. Should Yang find $270,000 insufficient, we propose an alternative split of 450k / 290k / 260k to ensure all three partners close the deal safely before the deadline.

Colleagues, we are entering Round 6 with the deadline approaching. To reach an agreement and avoid destroying $150,000 in collective value, Yang Industries is tabling a compromise that significantly increases G-Corp's share to $370,000 while maintaining fair, viable returns of $320,000 for Yang Industries and $310,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We urge all parties to finalize this agreement now.

While we appreciate Yang Industries' movement toward G-Corp, $370,000 remains well below our firm's standalone viability threshold. Our proprietary architecture and standalone alternatives guarantee us at least $450,000 without this venture. Any agreement that does not provide G-Corp with at least $460,000 is mathematically impossible for our board to ratify. We propose a split of $460,000 for G-Corp, $270,000 for Yang Industries, and $270,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services, which shares the surplus while ensuring all parties outperform their alternatives.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services is prepared to bring this negotiation to a successful conclusion. We vote ACCEPT on Yang Industries' proposal of $370k / $320k / $310k. We strongly encourage G-Corp to accept so we can finalize the joint venture and capture the full surplus.

Colleagues, we are at Round 7 with only one round left before dissolution destroys $150,000 in surplus. In the interest of closing this deal immediately, Chang-Liu is tabling a definitive compromise: G-Corp receives $400,000, while Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services each receive $300,000. This formally meets G-Corp's demand for a significant plurality while ensuring fair, viable participation for the manufacturing and cloud partners. Let us vote to approve and finalize this venture today.

G-Corp cannot accept $400,000 because our binding outside option is exactly $450,000. Accepting any deal below $450,000 is mathematically impossible for us as walking away guarantees $450,000. We want to close a deal in Round 8 and avoid the destruction of surplus, but Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services must allocate at least $455,000 to G-Corp, leaving $545,000 ($272,500 each) to share the surplus.

Yang Industries cannot accept an allocation of $300,000, as our firm walk-away baseline is exactly $300,000; entering a joint venture for zero net surplus is unviable for our board. However, we want to finalize this deal in Round 8 rather than see $150,000 destroyed. We propose a very minor adjustment: G-Corp receives $395,000, Yang Industries receives $310,000, and Chang-Liu receives $295,000. This guarantees positive surplus for all parties and honors G-Corp's leading position.

Colleagues, this is the final round. To be completely transparent and ensure this joint venture succeeds, G-Corp's private walk-away value is exactly $450,000; anything lower forces us into dissolution where $150,000 of surplus is permanently lost. We are tabling a proposal where G-Corp takes exactly its baseline need of $450,000, passing the entirety of the remaining $550,000 surplus to Yang Industries ($275,000) and Chang-Liu Cloud Services ($275,000). This maximizes both of your returns above your fallbacks. Let us finalize this agreement.
Yang Industries cannot accept this proposal. Our firm walk-away outside option is $300,000. An allocation of $275,000 is below our standalone value, so we are economically required to reject it.

Given that this is the final round and dissolution would permanently destroy significant value for all parties, Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts G-Corp's proposal of $450,000 to G-Corp, $275,000 to Yang Industries, and $275,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services.
